messages:
maya: heads-up — getting a customer escalation for /v1/generate p99 spike in eu-west-1 starting ~2024-09-19T10:12Z. p50 steady (~80ms) but p99 jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.8s. request rate unchanged. dashboard: https://console.redwood/insights/cluster-gamma/p99 (open to infra)
sam: thanks. any recent infra changes this morning? kernel/driver/firmware? also any background jobs scheduled around 10:00?
maya: we had a small rolling agent update at 03:00 UTC but the big change was a driver rollout (NVIDIA driver 525.85 -> 526.10) that started 2024-09-18 22:40 UTC and finished in eu-west-1 by ~02:30. host kernel 5.15.0-102 -> 5.15.0-104 was queued and rolled on a subset (20%) at 09:50 to test. Also backup snapshots start at 10:00 daily, hitting NVMe on those hosts.
lee: i'm seeing matching signals on the node-level metrics: NVMe util spikes and queue depth up on affected hosts. graph: https://graphs.redwood/nvme/queue-depth?host=gamma-03..07
diana: can we repro? i'll run a synthetic load to a single host behind the same LB target and sample header X-Instance to route to the host.
maya: repro steps I used:
```
# curl to specific instance
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -H "X-Instance-ID: gamma-03" -d '{"input":"token test"}' https://api.redwood/v1/generate
# run 50 concurrent requests with vegeta or hey
hey -n 500 -c 50 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -H "X-Instance-ID: gamma-03" https://api.redwood/v1/generate
```
results: p99 on gamma-03 ~1.7s. when I route to gamma-11 (not in driver roll) p99 430ms.
sam: good repro. can we grab iostat / nvme stats and dmesg from gamma-03?
lee: pasted iostat from gamma-03 at spike:
```
Device:         r/s   w/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  rMB/s  wMB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await  r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1       120.5  320.2    0.0    0.0   9.60  45.50    170.3    12.7   18.4   10.2   21.1    0.80  99.9
```
and dmesg tail:
```
[ 12345.678901] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout, latency 2000ms
[ 12345.679012] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
```
lee: NVMe %util ~100% during the window. backups are heavy writes to same device. that lines up w backups starting at 10:00.
oncall-eng: infra-bot alert: "p99 /v1/generate > 1s in eu-west-1 (cluster-gamma)" — triggered at 2024-09-19T10:14Z
maya: interestingly the kernel-rolled hosts show worse I/O latency even after driver rollback on some nodes. i suspect a combined effect: driver update changed submission path and kernel tweak changed I/O scheduler behavior, backups saturate NVMe, causing tail latency for token streaming (small sync writes from runtime to disk for kv-cache/metrics?).
diana: are there any disk throttles or cgroups for background jobs? we should throttle snapshots or move them to cold pool.
sam: immediate mitigations we can try (short list):
- pause daily backups on affected AZ for 30m
- divert traffic away from affected hosts (mark them draining in LB)
- rollout driver rollback to remaining updated hosts and verify
- apply io latency qdisc or set `nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us` ? (need careful testing)
- route heavy customers to fallback model-variant (lower mem, stateless) to reduce NVMe usage
maya: i'm pausing snapshots on eu-west-1 for 20m now (api call to snapshot-scheduler) — will post when done.
lee: in parallel i'm cordoning gamma-03..07 and moving active instances to gamma-11..15. LB weight adjust executed.

--- 9:58 UTC (after pausing backups & draining) ---

maya: quick numbers after pause + drain: p99 dropped to ~520ms on previously affected hosts. still slightly above baseline but huge improvement from 1.8s. cpu/gpu utilization unchanged.
sam: that suggests backups were dominant. let's still track driver/kernel signals. did anyone roll back the driver on a host and measure?
lee: rolled back driver on gamma-05 (one host) at 10:30, here's before/after for synthetic:
- before (driver 526.10): p99 1.6s
- after (525.85): p99 560ms
so rollback improves tail but not completely normal when backups running.
diana: good evidence driver+IO load interplay. root cause likely I/O path changes in new driver interacting with kernel I/O scheduler. next steps:
1) schedule full driver rollback for eu-west-1 (staged) but only after backups window cleared
2) add IO cgroup for snapshot process to cap write bandwidth (throttle to 100MB/s)
3) mark snapshots to write to backup pool on cold nodes (move to non-inference nvme pool)
4) add a short-term routing rule: if p99 > 800ms route to "fast-lite" variant
5) long-term: run driver+kernel integration matrix on lab fleet with heavy NVMe write mix

sam: action items assigned:
- @lee: apply IO throttling cgroup and complete staged driver rollback across remaining updated hosts (coordinate with oncall-eng) — ETA 2h
- @maya: keep drift dashboard / customer comms, confirm snapshot pause window and plan for snapshot reschedule — ETA 30m
- @diana: create runbook steps for snapshot cgroup + route fallback and PR to infra repo — ETA 4h
- @oncall-eng: keep paging policy open if p99 > 1s again, escalate to platform-eng if rollback doesn't help — immediate

infra-bot: deploybot: "driver-rollback/eu-west-1: batch-2 completed on 3 hosts" (logs: https://deploys.redwood/driver-rollback/17321)
maya: customer notified: temporary mitigations applied (draining, paused backups). apologized and offered reduced SLA credit if they see continued regressions. they asked for timeline for permanent fix; I gave estimated 48-72h for rolling thorough validation.
lee: note for postmortem: capture nvme SMART and firmware versions on impacted hosts. also collect perf counters for nvme submission latency and kernel blk_mq histograms.
diana: adding steps to incident ticket: repro commands, logs, iostat, dmesg snippet, mitigation timeline, owner list. ticket: https://support.redwood/tickets/INC-2024-0919-42
maya: good. i'll follow up with regression test in staging: reproduce driver+kernel+nvme write mix with long-running streaming to catch tail effects.
sam: if anyone sees p99 > 1s again in eu-west ping this channel immediately. thanks team — nice coordinated response. :thumbsup:
maya: closing the thread for now but will update once rollback and cgroup changes are fully rolled out.
summary: Customer reported p99 spike to 1.8s. Investigation showed NVMe saturation coincident with driver+kernel changes and daily backups. Immediate mitigations: pause backups, drain affected hosts, staged driver rollback; plan: IO cgroup for snapshots, move backups to cold pool, add routing fallback, lab validation.
